drafts.subject: chr:entity:mark-antony
drafts.quotation: But Antony, when the enemy sailed against him at daybreak, was afraid lest they should capture his ships while they had no fighting crews, and therefore armed the rowers and drew them up on the decks so as to make a show; then he grouped his ships at the mouth of the gulf near Actium
drafts.rationale: Antony is named as the one who arms the rowers and draws up his ships at the mouth of the gulf near Actium. This shows him directing the whole fleet, and no wing or centre is singled out, so the whole-fleet entity is the most specific one the passage supports.
drafts.relevance: It shows Antony's command of his fleet at Actium as the enemy approached.
ambiguities: The passage describes a stratagem as the enemy sailed up, not the main engagement itself, so it does not by itself show Antony taking part in the battle.
